transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
Hello doctor. Ever since the wreck two weeks ago, I just can’t think straight long enough to do my work or make simple decisions. It’s like my mind keeps stalling out.

Did these thinking and concentration problems start immediately after the wreck, or did they begin later and keep getting worse? Also, have they been steadily improving, staying the same, or getting worse over the past two weeks?

They started immediately, right after the crash two weeks ago, and it hasn't gotten any better at all. It's just been constantly like this every single day, and I'm so exhausted from my mind feeling completely stuck.
Since the crash, have you also had symptoms like feeling emotionally numb, being on edge or startled easily, having flashbacks or nightmares, or avoiding reminders of the accident?

Yes, I feel completely flat and disconnected, like even good news from my family just bounces right off me. I'm also constantly on edge, scanning the room, and if my wife walks in without me hearing her first, I jump so hard I almost fly out of my chair with my heart racing.

Have your symptoms been getting better at all since the accident, or have they stayed exactly the same every day for the full two weeks? Also, have you had any periods where you felt mostly back to normal before this crash?

No, they haven't improved at all and have stayed exactly this bad every single day since the accident. Before the crash, I was completely normal, easily managing my tax consulting business and enjoying my weekend fishing routine without any of these problems.
Have these symptoms continued for more than one month since the accident, or have they stayed limited to the first few weeks after it?
The accident actually only happened two weeks ago, so it hasn't been a full month yet. It has just been going on constantly for these past two weeks since the wreck.
Have these symptoms continued for more than one month since the accident, or are they still limited to the first few weeks after it?
Like I mentioned, the crash only happened two weeks ago, so it hasn't been a full month yet. These symptoms have just been going on constantly during these past two weeks.
Have you had any nightmares, flashbacks, or unwanted memories of the crash that keep coming back as if it is happening again?

No, I haven't really had nightmares or vivid flashbacks of the crash itself. Instead of re-experiencing it, my mind actually feels blank about a big part of the accident. Mostly, I just feel constantly on edge and disconnected from everything.
Has it been less than one month since the accident, or have these symptoms continued for more than one month?
Yes, it has been less than a month. The accident happened exactly two weeks ago, and these symptoms have been going on constantly ever since.
Have your symptoms been present for more than one month since the accident, or are they still within the first month after it?
They are still within the first month. Since the accident happened exactly two weeks ago, it hasn't even been a full month yet.
Have your symptoms been present for more than one month since the accident, or are they still within the first month after it?
Yes, they are definitely still within the first month. The crash was only two weeks ago, so it has been exactly two weeks of dealing with this constantly.
Since the accident, do you have repeated intrusive memories, nightmares, or flashbacks that make you feel like the crash is happening again?
No, I haven't had any nightmares or flashbacks where it feels like the crash is happening all over again. While I can remember the crash itself clearly, I'm not re-experiencing it in those ways.
Since the crash, have you had any periods where you felt detached from yourself or your surroundings, like things around you were unreal or you were watching yourself from outside your body?

Yes, especially when I'm riding in a car or passing the intersection where it happened, everything suddenly feels weirdly far away and fake. It feels like I'm watching a movie of my own life, just sort of floating a few feet behind my body instead of actually being inside it.
Have these symptoms lasted for more than one month since the accident, or are they still only within the first month after it?
As I've mentioned, the accident was only two weeks ago, so these symptoms are still within the first month. They have just been going on constantly for these past two weeks.
Have you had any of these symptoms for more than one month since the accident, or are they still only within the first month after it?
No, it hasn't been a month yet because the wreck only happened two weeks ago. All of these symptoms have just been going on constantly since that night.

Have your symptoms been steadily improving since the accident, or have they stayed severe and unchanging? Acute stress disorder usually improves within days to weeks, while PTSD symptoms tend to persist longer and often include re-experiencing the trauma.
They haven't improved at all, doctor; they have stayed severe and completely unchanging since the wreck two weeks ago. It is still just as hard to think straight or function as it was on day one.
Do you have repeated intrusive memories, nightmares, or flashbacks that make you feel like the crash is happening again?

No, I really don't experience nightmares or flashbacks where I feel like the crash is happening all over again. I can still picture the truck spinning in my mind when I think about it, but I don't have those specific bad dreams or intrusive episodes.
Do you get unwanted, intrusive memories of the crash that suddenly come back and feel like it is happening again, or are your symptoms mainly numbness, being on edge, and feeling detached?

No, I don't get those flashbacks where it feels like the crash is happening again. My symptoms are definitely more about feeling completely flat and numb, constantly being jumpy and on edge, and feeling detached from everything like it's all fake. It really does feel like I'm just watching a movie of my own life.
Do you have repeated intrusive memories, nightmares, or flashbacks that make it feel like the crash is happening again, or are your symptoms mainly feeling numb, on edge, and detached?

No, I don't have nightmares or flashbacks where it feels like the crash is happening again. It's definitely more about feeling flat and disconnected from everything, and constantly being on edge, scanning rooms and jumping at any sudden noise. Sometimes things feel so fake that it's like I'm just watching a movie of my own life.
Since the accident, do you try to avoid places, people, driving routes, or reminders of the crash because they make you feel distressed?
I haven't really been actively trying to avoid places, routes, or reminders of the crash. To be honest, I haven't really thought about it, so I don't think I've been doing that.

Since the accident, have you had any moments of feeling confused about where you are, unable to remember parts of what happened, or feeling like you were in a daze and not fully aware of what was going on around you?

Yes, I have a big empty hole in my memory between seeing the headlights and suddenly being outside on the stretcher, and I can't recall what happened in those minutes. Also, especially when I'm in a car or near the crash site, I get in this daze where everything feels fake and far away, like I'm watching myself in a movie rather than being in my own body.
Have these symptoms continued for more than one month since the accident, or are they still only within the first month after it?
They are still within the first month, as the accident only happened two weeks ago. These symptoms have just been going on constantly for these past two weeks.
Have these symptoms lasted for more than one month since the accident, or are they still only within the first month after it?
They are definitely still within the first month, since the wreck only happened two weeks ago. It has just been these past two weeks that I've been dealing with all of this constantly.

Have your symptoms been steadily improving at all since the accident, or have they stayed severe and unchanged? Acute stress disorder usually improves within days to weeks, while PTSD symptoms persist longer.

They haven't gotten any better at all and have stayed just as severe and constant since the accident two weeks ago. It’s incredibly frustrating because I keep hoping for some relief, but absolutely nothing has improved since it happened.
